    Global dimension at most two (proof of Proposition 2.10) #

    "At a nonprojective label X, the exact right mesh … give 0 → R_{τX} → ⊕_{Y→X} R_Y → R_X → L_X → 0. At a projective label P, the same lemma gives a resolution 0 → R_{rad P} → R_P → L_P → 0 of length at most one. Hence gl.dim Λ ≤ 2." The proof of Lemma 2.9 uses this in the form "its kernel is a second syzygy and hence projective".

    We derive this consequence: every finite-dimensional module has a projective resolution of length two by modules R_Z (the simple resolutions and the horseshoe construction, along a composition series); by Schanuel's lemma every second syzygy is projective; a finite-dimensional projective module is some R_W (tops and Nakayama's lemma).

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.

        One horseshoe step. Let 0 → A' → A → A'' → 0 be exact (i injective, p surjective, ker p = range i) and let e' : P' → A', e'' : P'' → A'' be surjections with P'' projective. Then e : P' × P'' → A, (a, b) ↦ i (e' a) + λ b with p λ = e'', is surjective, and its kernel is an extension of ker e'' by ker e'.
